ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached image shows a Ksp table with columns Name, Formula, and Ksp. The listed compounds are cadmium carbonate (CdCO3, 5.2 × 10^-12), cadmium hydroxide (Cd(OH)2, 2.5 × 10^-14), calcium fluoride (CaF2, 3.9 × 10^-11), silver iodide (AgI, 8.3 × 10^-17), and zinc carbonate (ZnCO3, 1.4 × 10^-11). Manganese hydroxide, Mn(OH)2, is not present in the table. Reasoning: From the question text, the molar solubility of Mn(OH)2 is s = 2.2 × 10^-5 M. The dissolution equation is Mn(OH)2(s) ⇌ Mn2+ + 2OH-. Therefore [Mn2+] = s = 2.2 × 10^-5 M and [OH-] = 2s = 4.4 × 10^-5 M. The solubility product is Ksp = [Mn2+][OH-]^2 = (2.2 × 10^-5)(4.4 × 10^-5)^2 = 4.2592 × 10^-14, which rounds to 4.3 × 10^-14.
